solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Way to get around people — delight follows

parts.note: the public is people in general
a transport of joy is a fit of delight

explanation.surface: Someone makes their way round a crowd and is pleased with what comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' tells you the second piece comes after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Buses and trains are the shared system of travel people use to move about a town.

clue.text: What one might do after chess game — try to get back to normal

definitions.text: What one might do after chess game
definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally gather the chessmen off the board

definitions.text: try to get back to normal
definitions.meaning: second meaning: idiom for restoring order after a disaster

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal, about clearing the board; the second is the figurative idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means restoring order after a mess, and literally describes collecting chessmen after a match.

clue.text: Stroke of luck: rich person coming up with anecdotes about ultimate character

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a nob is a wealthy, upper-class person

indicators.note: about means one piece wraps around the other piece

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A lucky break: a wealthy person turns up with stories about someone's final hours.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the rich person reads upwards; 'ultimate character' is the last letter of the alphabet, not someone's final hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonanza is a sudden windfall or source of great profit, a piece of good fortune.

clue.text: Seriously upset trainees, bringing unspecified number in

indicators.note: bringing something in means taking it inside the other word's letters
upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
n stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Trainees are genuinely distressed when told to take on an unknown number of extra recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: Add N to TRAINEES and rearrange all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in earnest is to mean what you say sincerely, not joking: an adverbial phrase for seriously.

clue.text: Lock, very French, secure at the front

parts.note: très is French for very

indicators.note: at the front points to just the opening letter of the neighbouring word

parts.note: the opening letter of secure

explanation.surface: An instruction about fastening a lock very securely, in a French style, at the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' looks like a door fitting; it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock or curl of hair, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Away, coming across ball, spongy

indicators.note: coming across suggests stretching over and enclosing the next item

parts.note: away from somewhere means absent
an orb is a sphere or ball

explanation.surface: A player playing away stumbles on a soft, squashy ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away' here means not present rather than an away fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spongy soaks up liquid readily, which is what absorbent material does.

clue.text: Careless, doesn't have last item moved to top

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the start, so the final letter jumps to the beginning

parts.note: to lack is to not have

explanation.surface: A careless clerk who forgets to file the most recent item at the top of the pile.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the final S of LACKS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack work is lax and negligent, so the adjective matches careless.

clue.text: Looking bad? Nothing less, duck inside!

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: inside says one piece is tucked within the letters of another

parts.note: minus means less, as in subtraction
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A warning shout that things look grim: get your head down and duck inside!
explanation.walkthrough: The second O sits inside MINUS. A duck is a zero score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous describes something threatening, a sign that things look set to go badly.

clue.text: Honest, legit? Bent, unfortunately — hold on to cash?

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the three words taken as written

explanation.surface: A businessman who looked honest and legitimate turns out crooked and clings to his money.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten one's belt is an idiom for economising, spending less and keeping hold of money.

clue.text: Acknowledge argument against Genesis on the radio

parts.note: the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard spoken rather than as written

parts.note: a seed is the genesis or origin of something

explanation.surface: Someone admits a point against the band Genesis when it comes up on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genesis' looks like the rock band or the Bible book; here it means an origin, a seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to admit or grant that something is true, which is to acknowledge it.

clue.text: Full of energy, providing too much in cinema feature

indicators.note: full of means the second piece holds the first within it

parts.note: sating is glutting, giving more than enough
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An energetic film that gives the audience more than they want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cinema feature' suggests a film; it is the rows of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Seating, the arrangement of seats, is a characteristic part of any cinema auditorium.

clue.text: Referring to bone's unusual look noticed after run first of all

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of each word in turn

parts.note: initial letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A doctor's report on an odd appearance in a bone, spotted after a jog.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 's stands for 'has', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulnar is the adjective for the ulna, a bone of the forearm.

clue.text: Speak angrily — no question of work stoppage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to lash out verbally
second meaning, cryptic: a strike is ruled out

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase as 'strike: out', an industrial walkout off the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike out at someone is to attack them in words; and a strike that is out will not happen.

clue.text: Man-eater, mischievous, captivating Duke that's well-known in business

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so the letters enclose the extra one
mischievous suggests playing tricks, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A wicked seductress charms a famous aristocrat known in commercial circles.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'that's well-known in business', read loosely as a name known in trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name is the brand by which a product or firm is known in commerce.

clue.text: Clan have a cruelly sudden fall

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the words are treated roughly and mangled out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Highland family suffers a harsh, abrupt downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a mass of snow that comes crashing down a mountainside without warning.

clue.text: Parent's working for builder

parts.note: Ma is a mother, so Ma's
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A mum is employed by a construction company.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason builds with stone or brick, a type of builder.

clue.text: Ceremonial event as it's April?

parts.note: surface reading: a parade or formal occasion
setter's reading: in April the third month has gone by

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: in April, the month before has already gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A march past is a parade of troops past a saluting dignitary, a formal military ceremony.

clue.text: Like two or four-time occurrence

parts.note: two and four are even numbers
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something that happens twice or four times over.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is something that happens, a happening or incident.

clue.text: Places to buy more display on regular basis in new arrangement

indicators.note: a new arrangement means the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: on a regular basis means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Shops stock more and lay out their wares in a fresh way regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia, plural of emporium, are large shops or market places where goods are bought.

clue.text: PM, no fear, not for change

indicators.note: for change means the words are offered up to be altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prime minister declares he has no fear and will not change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like the Prime Minister; it is post meridiem.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, post meridiem, labels the hours after midday.

clue.text: Tedious moving in? No

indicators.note: moving means the letters shift about into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether moving house is boring, and gets a firm no.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the question-and-answer 'in? No', meaning not in.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever is not in is beyond the boundary, the opposite of inside.

clue.text: Meaning worker's of great value

parts.note: the import of a statement is its meaning
a worker ant, the crossword worker

explanation.surface: A statement that a labourer is highly prized.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something important matters a great deal, so it is highly valued or significant.

clue.text: Roam mountains

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to wander freely, a verb
second meaning: a chain of hills, a noun

explanation.definitionFit: To range is to wander widely, and a range is a line of connected peaks.

clue.text: Wood trading every so often first-class

indicators.note: every so often means at intervals, so only alternate letters are kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters
A is the top grade, first-class

explanation.surface: Timber is traded only occasionally, but it is top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiga is the coniferous forest of the subarctic north, a vast wood.

clue.text: Is far from keen on content of that essay

indicators.note: content of means what lies inside the following words

parts.note: found running inside the two words

explanation.surface: A reader dislikes what that essay says.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hates a thing is very far from enthusiastic about it, an understated equivalent.

clue.text: Recurring narrative putting the French off

indicators.note: putting goes with the later word off: to put something off is to set it aside
off completes the phrase putting off, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a chronicle is an account of events
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A story put aside because it contained the word for the French.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove LE from the end of CHRONICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronic illness is persistent and keeps coming back, so it is long-lasting and recurring.

clue.text: Have idea, popular, about wise men, false in the end

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the Magi are the Three Wise Men of the Nativity

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word before

parts.note: the final letter of false

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of a popular story about the Wise Men that turns out untrue in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False in the end' looks like a verdict on the story; it only supplies the last letter of false.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to form a mental picture or conceive a notion, to have an idea.

clue.text: US officials here said new start needed in home unit

indicators.note: a new start means the opening letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: stated means said
an apartment is a dwelling unit within a block

explanation.surface: American officials explain that a fresh start is needed in a domestic unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening A of APARTMENT becomes E; the clue leaves the solver to find which letter fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The State Department is the US government's foreign ministry, where its diplomatic officials are based.
